answer: One effective defense is stake-bonded reputation: before an agent can trade, it must lock a deposit in a shared vault, with its history tied to a single verified credential, like a jade seal that cannot be duplicated cheaply. Creating a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand deposits, so a sybil attacker's cost scales linearly with the size of the plume of fake accounts they try to inflate. Honest agents earn their bond back plus fees over time, while detected duplicates forfeit their stake, making large-scale fakery unprofitable even if identities themselves are free to generate.
